title: An ample line module realizes every homogeneous class as a translation difference
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $M$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-sc-ample, def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module such that $t_b^*L\cong L$ for every $b\in A(k)$, where $t_b(x)=x+b$ is translation in $A$. Then there is $a\in A(k)$ with $$L\cong t_a^*M\otimes_{\mathcal O_A}M^{-1}.$$ Here pullbacks are tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback], tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $M^{-1}=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_A}(M,\mathcal O_A)$ is the dual invertible module. No restriction on the characteristic of $k$ or the dimension of $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Chapter I §8, Proposition 8.14, printed p.39, with the definition of Pic^0(A) by the equivalent conditions of Proposition 8.4(b), printed pp.35–36; lambda_M(a)=t_a^*M tensor M^{-1}, printed p.34. This uses the homogeneous definition of Pic^0, not an assumption identifying it with algebraic equivalence.

proof.text: By [def-sc-abelian-variety] and [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], $A$ is nonempty, proper, smooth and geometrically integral. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the relative dimension is locally constant, hence constant on connected $A$; denote it $g\geq0$. The group law is commutative by [lem-sc-av-commutative]. By [def-sc-ample] choose $r\geq1$ such that $B=M^{\otimes r}$ is very ample. The defining closed immersion $i:A\to\mathbf P^N_k$, with $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong B$, makes $A$ projective, and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible], applied to $i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $B$ ample in the absolute sense of Stacks 01PS needed for twisting. By [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], $\Omega^1_{A/k}$ is locally free of rank $g$, so its top exterior power $\omega=\bigwedge^g\Omega^1_{A/k}$ is invertible: in each frame the top wedge is one generator, and its change-of-frame scalar is the determinant, a unit. This includes $g=0$, when $\omega=\mathcal O_A$. By [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], $\mathcal O_A$ and $\omega\otimes L$ are coherent; tensoring their rank-one local frames shows that $\omega\otimes L$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0FVV, lemma-duality-proper-over-field (7); smooth differential rank is Morphisms Tag 02G1; the ample-power convention is the statement of def-sc-ample.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] to the absolutely ample $B$ and separately to $\mathcal O_A$ and $\omega\otimes L$. Choose a common integer $q\geq1$ beyond both bounds and set $n=rq$ and $N=M^{\otimes n}=B^{\otimes q}$. Then $N$ and $\omega\otimes N\otimes L$ are globally generated. Each has a nonzero fibre at the identity $0\in A(k)$, and evaluation of the finite generating family surjects onto that fibre. Consequently at least one generating section has nonzero value there. Thus both $H^0(A,N)$ and $H^0(A,\omega\otimes N\otimes L)$ are nonzero.

source.place: Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample, clause (7): sufficiently positive twists of a finite type quasi-coherent module are globally generated.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-projective-line-module-serre-duality] on the smooth projective pure-$g$ scheme $A$ and the invertible module $E=\omega\otimes N\otimes L$. Its assertion at $j=g$ gives $$H^g(A,N^{-1}\otimes L^{-1})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^0(A,\omega\otimes N\otimes L),k)\ne0,$$ since $\omega\otimes E^\vee\cong N^{-1}\otimes L^{-1}$ in local rank-one frames. The cohomology is finite dimensional by that node, so the dual of the nonzero space in step 2 is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0FVV, lemma-duality-proper-over-field (5),(7), and Tag 0FW0, remark-rework-duality-locally-free-CM, specialized to an invertible module.

proof.text: Let $m:A\times_kA\to A$ be addition and $p_1,p_2$ the projections. Write $D_b=t_b^*N\otimes N^{-1}$. For $a,b\in A(k)$ pull the identity of [thm-sc-theorem-of-cube] for $N$ back along $x\mapsto(x,a,b)$, $A\to A\times_kA\times_kA$. By composition [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] the partial sums $m_{123},m_1,m_{12},m_{13}$ become $t_{a+b},\mathrm{id},t_a,t_b$, and $m_2,m_3,m_{23}$ become the constant maps with values $a,b,a+b$, which factor through $\operatorname{Spec}k$; there an invertible module is a one-dimensional vector space, so these three pullbacks are trivial. With tensor pullback [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] this is the theorem of the square $t_{a+b}^*N\otimes N\cong t_a^*N\otimes t_b^*N$, valid for every invertible module; thus $D_{a+b}\cong D_a\otimes D_b$. The same rules give $$t_a^*D_b\otimes D_b^{-1}\cong t_{a+b}^*N\otimes(t_a^*N)^{-1}\otimes(t_b^*N)^{-1}\otimes N\cong\mathcal O_A.$$ Thus $D_b$ is homogeneous, and so is $D_b\otimes L^{-1}$ by the hypothesis on $L$ and the same tensor rules. Form the invertible module $$\mathcal F=m^*N\otimes p_1^*(N^{-1}\otimes L^{-1})$$ on $A\times_k A$. Its fibre over $b$ for $p_2$ is $D_b\otimes L^{-1}$. Suppose for contradiction that every such fibre is nontrivial. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-coherent-acyclicity], $H^i(A,\mathcal F_b)=0$ for every $i\geq0$ and every $b\in A(k)$. No identification of homogeneous with algebraically trivial classes is used.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 5.5 (theorem of the square) with its proof from the cube via Corollary 5.3, printed pp.22–23; Remark 5.6 and §8, printed p.34; Proposition 8.4(b), printed pp.35–36; cohomological contradiction supplied by the agent.

proof.text: The projection $p_2$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability], smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], and flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Properness adds quasi-compactness and separatedness, so it is of finite presentation. The line module $\mathcal F$ is finitely presented and flat over the second factor: in local frames it is $\mathcal O_{A\times A}$. Therefore [lem-pc-universal-finite-free-complex] supplies locally on $A$ a finite free complex $P$ in $[0,d]$ computing all $R^ip_{2*}\mathcal F$ and, after every base change, the fibre cohomology. Every closed point of $A$ has residue field $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], so $P\otimes k(b)$ is exact there by step 4.

source.place: Tags 0B91, lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general, and 0A1H, lemma-base-change-tensor-perfect; the universal finite free complex is the cited node’s explicit statement.

proof.text: At a closed point $b$, exactness of $P\otimes k(b)$ makes its last differential surjective. Choose a square minor of size the rank of the last term with nonzero determinant at $b$, and invert its determinant on a neighbourhood. Row and column operations split off the identity complex in the last two degrees. Repeat for the remaining shorter complex; there are finitely many terms. In the final degree zero, exactness of the residue complex forces the rank of the surviving free term to be zero. Thus $P$ is contractible on some neighbourhood of $b$, and all $R^ip_{2*}\mathcal F$ vanish there. These neighbourhoods cover $A$: if their union had nonempty closed complement, [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] would give a closed point in that complement, a contradiction. Hence $R^ip_{2*}\mathcal F=0$ on all of $A$ for every $i\geq0$. This is just finite-matrix cancellation applied to the universal complex of the previous step.

source.place: Elementary cancellation of a bounded finite free complex at an exact residue fibre, applied to the complex of step 5; closed-point detection uses the cited Jacobson-space statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-leray-spectral-sequence] to $p_2$ on the Zariski ringed sites. Step 6 makes its entire $E_2$ page zero, and the finite abutment filtrations give $H^i(A\times_kA,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $i\geq0$. On the other hand the group law defines an isomorphism $u:A\times_kA\to A\times_kA$, $u(x,b)=(x,x+b)$, with inverse $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y-x)$. Set $G=N^{-1}\otimes L^{-1}$ and $\mathcal E=p_1^*G\otimes p_2^*N$. Then $p_1u=p_1$ and $p_2u=m$, so the pullback tensor and composition identities give $u^*\mathcal E\cong\mathcal F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial], pullback along $u$ and its displayed inverse are mutually inverse on cohomology (use its composition and identity clauses with the canonical coefficient comparisons). Consequently $H^i(A\times_kA,\mathcal E)=0$ for all $i\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 0732, lemma-Leray; coordinate-change calculation and the contradiction are agent supplied.

proof.text: Both factors $A$ are quasi-compact and separated because they are proper. Their diagonals are closed immersions, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc](b). The invertible modules $G,N$ are quasi-coherent. Thus [lem-sc-picard-kunneth-qcoh] applies and gives $$H^g(A\times_kA,\mathcal E)\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=g}H^i(A,G)\otimes_kH^j(A,N).$$ Its $(i,j)=(g,0)$ summand is nonzero by steps 2 and 3: nonzero vectors in vector spaces over a field have nonzero pure tensor, as extending them to bases shows. This contradicts step 7. Hence for some $b\in A(k)$ the fibre $D_b\otimes L^{-1}$ is trivial, or $L\cong t_b^*N\otimes N^{-1}$. This argument also covers $g=0$, with summand $(0,0)$.

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth, coherent Kunneth formula over a field; nonzero summand contradiction is agent supplied.

proof.text: Tensor pullback [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] identifies $t_b^*(M^{\otimes n})\otimes(M^{\otimes n})^{-1}$ with $(t_b^*M\otimes M^{-1})^{\otimes n}$. The theorem of the square of step 4, obtained from [thm-sc-theorem-of-cube] and pullback composition [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] for any invertible module and here applied to $M$, gives $t_{(j+1)b}^*M\otimes M^{-1}\cong(t_{jb}^*M\otimes M^{-1})\otimes(t_b^*M\otimes M^{-1})$ for every $j\geq0$; induction on $j$ identifies the latter module with $t_{nb}^*M\otimes M^{-1}$. Take $a=nb\in A(k)$. The isomorphism at the end of step 8 now yields exactly $L\cong t_a^*M\otimes M^{-1}$. No extraction of an $n$th root and no division by $n$ in $k$ occurs.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 5.5 and Remark 5.6, printed pp.22–23 (a ↦ t_a^*M⊗M^{-1} is a homomorphism); tensor-power calculation completing Proposition 8.14.

proof_origin.place: I Proposition 8.14 states the result but refers its proof to Mumford §8 p.77 or Lang p.99 (WANTED). The present cohomological proof is agent supplied, using homogeneous acyclicity, positive twists, Serre duality, universal finite free complexes and coherent Kunneth.
